handoff.purpose: Implement Selection, BeforeState, CorrectnessResult, freeze_selection, _check_selection, judge_before_state, judge_after_state, _run_lists, and the beginning of evaluate_change.

symbols.name: Selection.digest
symbols.note: Returns first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 hash of JSON-serialized selection fields.

symbols.name: freeze_selection
symbols.note: Creates an immutable Selection from a task dict, with deduplication and sorting.

symbols.name: _check_selection
symbols.note: Guards that observed test nodes match the frozen selection; returns error string if not.

symbols.name: BeforeState
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing test results on base revision.

symbols.name: judge_before_state
symbols.note: Pure function that determines if the before-state is valid, unrunnable, or invalid.

symbols.name: CorrectnessResult
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing one evaluation outcome.

symbols.name: CorrectnessResult.ok
symbols.note: Returns True only when outcome is OUTCOME_FIXED.

symbols.name: judge_after_state
symbols.note: Pure function that determines outcome after the change.

symbols.name: _run_lists
symbols.note: Runs FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS as separate invocations.

claims.text: Node ids are taken EXACTLY as declared -- deduplicated and ordered for determinism, never expanded, never filtered, and never read from the filesystem.
claims.why: The function uses dict.fromkeys for dedup, sorted for ordering, and only reads from the task dict; no filesystem access.

claims.text: A set that could grow to match something a candidate added is not a frozen set, and this function is the only place a set is ever built for an evaluation.
claims.why: The claim about being the only place is not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: A runner is injectable, and a gate is a subprocess whose output is parsed; either could in principle report a node that is not in the frozen set.
claims.why: The injectable runner and gate are not defined in this chunk; the claim is conceptual.

claims.text: A result computed over a set that is not the declared one is not the measurement that was declared, so it is refused rather than reported.
claims.why: The function returns an error string if observed nodes differ from declared; it does not return a result.

claims.text: verified is True only when every FAIL_TO_PASS node was PROVEN not to pass and every PASS_TO_PASS node passed.
claims.why: judge_before_state returns verified=True only if no bad_f2p and no bad_p2p.

claims.text: Anything else is either an invalid task or an unobtainable verdict, and reasons says which.
claims.why: judge_before_state returns invalid=True or unrunnable=True with reasons.

claims.text: NO VERDICT (not_run) -> unrunnable. An unknown never becomes a fact in either direction.
claims.why: If unknown nodes exist, function returns BeforeState with unrunnable=True.

claims.text: A claimed FAIL_TO_PASS node that PASSED, was SKIPPED, or is MISSING -> invalid. Passing refutes the claim outright; skipped is not evidence of failure; missing means the node id does not exist even with the test overlay applied.
claims.why: The function checks for STATUS_PASSED, STATUS_MISSING, and other non-PROVEN_NOT_PASSING statuses and adds reasons.

claims.text: A claimed PASS_TO_PASS node that did not pass -> invalid.
claims.why: The function checks for any status not equal to STATUS_PASSED and marks invalid.

claims.text: True only for fixed. Nothing else is a pass, including could_not_run -- especially could_not_run.

claims.why: The function checks unknown first, then regressed, then unfixed, then returns fixed.

claims.text: A change that breaks the regression set is reported as breaking it EVEN IF it also turned every FAIL_TO_PASS green
claims.why: The function checks regressed before fixed/unfixed; if regressed exists, it returns OUTCOME_REGRESSED regardless of fixed.

claims.text: Two invocations on purpose: a collection error in one list must not turn the other list into not_run
claims.why: The function runs f2p and p2p separately; if one fails, the other still runs.

claims.text: Takes the frozen Selection, NOT the task dict, and that is the structural half of the immutability rule: once a selection is frozen there is no code path left that can consult the task for node ids again
claims.why: The chunk does not show whether other code paths consult the task dict; the function itself takes a Selection.

observations.what: The digest property uses import hashlib inside the method; this is unusual but not incorrect.
freeze_selection sets gate='pytest' unconditionally; the task's gate field is ignored.
judge_before_state constructs the unknown list from both f2p and p2p, but the docstring says 'an unknown never becomes a fact in either direction'; the code matches.
In judge_after_state, the 'unknown' check uses {**after_f2p, **after_p2p} which creates a merged dict; this is correct.
